name: Record the admission test score against the applicant
priorityReason: The admission decision reads the score. Without it recorded, nothing downstream can proceed.

goal.capability: to record what an applicant scored against the right applicant
goal.outcome: the admission decision rests on something recorded rather than a paper on someone's desk

secondaryActors.involvement: Conducts the test and marks the paper. May record the score directly.
The applicant sits the test on the scheduled date.
Read the score alongside the admission form when deciding.

additional.description: The scheduled test date and time pass, and the applicant appears in the marker's list awaiting a score.
A test taken but unmarked past the configured target is escalated to the Coordinator (BR-9).

preconditions.condition: An applicant exists with a temporary ID and a scheduled test.
A maximum mark is configured for the admission test of that class, so a score can be validated (BR-3).
The scheduled date and time have passed, or the applicant has been marked absent.

postConditions: The applicant carries either a score or an Absent result, recorded against their temporary ID, with who marked it and when.
The score and the completed admission form are both visible to School Admin and Principal, which is what the admission decision reads.
An applicant recorded absent carries no score at all, so the decision reads a no-show differently from a poor result.
The applicant is ready for eligibility flagging; no eligibility, admission or rejection has been decided here.
Any correction to a recorded score keeps its previous value in the audit trail, since a score is the basis of an admission decision.

dataFields.name: Applicant
dataFields.validation: Identified by temporary ID. The score attaches to that identifier and nothing else (BR-1).

dataFields.name: Attendance
dataFields.validation: Recorded before any score. An absent applicant carries no score (BR-4).

dataFields.name: Score
dataFields.validation: A whole number from 0 to the maximum mark configured for that class's test. Refused outside the range (BR-3).

dataFields.name: Maximum mark
dataFields.validation: Configured per class, shown alongside the score so the marker knows the range.

dataFields.name: Marker remark
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Visible to School Admin and Principal, never to the family (BR-8).
dataFields.example: Strong in English, weak in numeracy.

dataFields.name: Marked by
dataFields.validation: The user who recorded the score.

dataFields.name: Correction reason
dataFields.validation: Maximum 250 characters. Required when changing a recorded score (BR-7).
dataFields.example: Second page of the paper was not marked.
dataFields.requiredWhen: A recorded score is being changed

entities.notes: Read for the scheduled test; updated with attendance, score and result.
One row per applicant, holding attendance, score, marker and remark. Corrections keep their history.
Read for the assigned marker; moved to Taken or Missed.
Every score entry and every correction, with the previous value.

permissions.notes: Records the score against the temporary ID on behalf of the marker.
Records attendance and the score for their own assigned tests. Cannot see other applicants.

permissions.rowScope: Own branch; may switch per branch-scope.
permissions.notes: Reads the score, and is the only role that may correct one after it has been read by the Principal (BR-7).

permissions.rowScope: No access. The result is communicated as part of the decision, not exposed here (BR-8).

businessRules.rule: The score is recorded against the applicant's temporary ID. A score recorded against the wrong applicant is the failure this rule exists to prevent, so the identifier is shown at every step.
Attendance is recorded before any score. The two are separate acts because a no-show and a poor result mean different things to the decision.
A score is validated against the maximum mark configured for that class's test, and a value outside 0 to the maximum is refused.
An applicant recorded absent carries no score at all — not a zero. Zero means they sat the test and scored nothing, which is a different fact.
The score is recorded, not judged. This use case sets no pass mark, decides no eligibility and admits nobody.
The score and the completed admission form become visible together to School Admin and Principal, because neither is enough on its own to decide an admission.
A recorded score may be corrected with a reason. The previous value stays in the audit trail, because an admission decision may already have been taken on it.
The marker's remark is internal. It is visible to School Admin and Principal and is never sent to the family.
A test taken but unmarked past the configured target is escalated to the Coordinator, so an applicant is not left waiting on a paper nobody marked.
An applicant who missed the test may be rescheduled rather than decided on. Missing a test is not a result.

transitions.condition: Attendance recorded as Absent. No score is held (BR-4).
A score within the maximum mark is recorded.
The score is changed with a reason (BR-7).
The corrected value stands as the score.

basicFlow.navigation: Arrives at the venue → Sits the test
basicFlow.userAction: The applicant sits the test at the scheduled date and time.
Opens their list for the day and records attendance for each applicant.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Sets the applicant to Test taken, or to Absent with no score held.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicants awaiting a score → Record test result
basicFlow.userAction: Opens the applicant by temporary ID and enters the score and any remark.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Validates the score against the maximum mark configured for that class's test.
Saves the score with the marker and the time, and sets the result to Marked.
Makes the score and the completed admission form visible together in the School Admin and Principal accounts.

alternateFlows.behaviour: The applicant is recorded Absent and carries no score. The decision reads a no-show differently from a poor result, and the applicant may be rescheduled rather than decided on (BR-4, BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The marking teacher records the score directly rather than handing it to Staff
alternateFlows.navigation: My admission tests → Record test result
alternateFlows.behaviour: The same screen and the same validation. Only the actor differs.

alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicant → Record test result → Correct score
alternateFlows.behaviour: The score is corrected with a reason. The previous value stays in the audit trail, because a decision may already have been taken on it (BR-7).

alternateFlows.condition: An absent applicant is given another chance
alternateFlows.navigation: Login → Inquiry / Admission → Applicant → Reschedule test
alternateFlows.behaviour: The applicant returns to Awaiting test and is scheduled again. The earlier absence stays in the history (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: A whole sitting is being marked at once
alternateFlows.navigation: My admission tests → Enter scores for the day
alternateFlows.behaviour: Scores for every applicant in that sitting are entered on one screen. Each is validated and saved individually, and one invalid entry does not discard the rest.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: academic-session-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every academic record carries an academic session ID. Lists default to the current open session.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: bulk-actions
conventionsApplied.rule: Any bulk operation reports a per-row result, commits valid rows and lists rejected rows with the reason. A bulk action never fails as a whole because of one bad row.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
